title: Adaptive observability for embed + rerank: route-level cost attribution and alerts
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Deliver a lightweight, adaptive observability layer for embeddings + reranking endpoints that provides: (1) route-level cost attribution (tokens, embeddings, vector ops), (2) sampled tracing across embed->vector-store->reranker hotpath, (3) per-route dashboards and alerting with adaptive thresholds to reduce noise and surface real regressions. This ticket covers instrumentation, dashboard templates, alert rules, and a staged rollout for 3 pilot routes.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route dashboard template available in Grafana and Console that shows: request rate, p50/p95 latency for embed and rerank stages, tokens/embedding units consumed, CPU/GPU utilization for the serving pool, and estimated $/hour cost for the route
Trace spans instrumented for: text->embedding compute, embedding->vector-store lookup (including KV cache hit/miss), reranker scoring step; spans include route ID and model variant metadata
Cost attribution produced at 1-minute granularity and exposed as a Prometheus metric and Console cost slice for chargeback

Adaptive alerting rules created: automatic baseline using 14-day rolling window and anomaly deviation; alerts trigger runbook with severity mapping (P0 if combined cost increase >25% and latency regression >15%)
Rollout to 3 pilot routes with fallback to global SLOs and opt-out via config; no significant telemetry-induced latency increase (<= 1% added p95 latency)
Documentation and runbook published with links to PRs, dashboards, and post-mortem templates
implementation_notes: Instrument embed and rerank code paths to emit structured metrics: embed_request_count, embed_latency_ms_bucket, embed_tokens, embedding_units, rerank_request_count, rerank_latency_ms_bucket, rerank_score_distribution
Add trace tags: route_id, model_name, model_variant, kv_cache_status (HIT|MISS), batch_size
Use 1% distributed tracing sampling global with 100% sampling for errors and high-latency (> p99) requests to limit overhead
Compute cost attribution by joining metrics: estimate GPU seconds per token/embedding using model profiles and multiply by GPU price to create cost_per_route metric
Dashboards use templated variables for route and model variant. Provide a smaller mobile-friendly view for on-call
Implement a lightweight aggregator (sidecar) to synthesize per-route cost every minute and push to Prometheus remote write to avoid query-time joins
Tradeoff: fine-grained per-token telemetry rejected due to high cardinality. We instead sample tokens for quality checks and compute aggregated estimates for cost

comments: PM note (Rachel Lee): Please ensure the alerting noise is minimized for low-traffic routes — prefer aggregated anomalies over single-sample spikes.
Design review (Linnea S): Dashboard should highlight cache miss hotspots; consider a heatmap for model-variant vs route latency.

Security (Omar Patel): Confirm no sensitive payload is stored in traces. We should redact prompt text and only store hashes. See security guideline: confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/Tracing+PII+Policy
Infra feedback (Jordan Miles): Sidecar approach ok for now; long-term we should move to streaming aggregation in the serving runtime to reduce tail latency and cross-node joins.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: instrumentation and dashboards in staging (complete)
Phase 1: pilot on 3 low-risk routes for one week with increased sampling (canary)
Phase 2: enable adaptive alerts for pilot routes; collect false-positive statistics
Phase 3: iterate thresholds and deploy to 20% of routes by traffic share
Phase 4: global rollout with runbook and billing integration
tradeoffs: Sampling traces reduces overhead but can miss correlated failures — mitigated by 100% error tracing and high-latency sampling
Sidecar aggregator reduces query-time complexity at the cost of additional components per node — acceptable short-term; evaluate runtime aggregation later
Estimating cost from model profiles introduces approximation error (~5-10%) but avoids high-cardinality per-request billing metrics
